increments.title: Mandatory members are created at any group depth
increments.goal: Recruiting a unit materialises every member the catalogue makes mandatory, however deeply the mandatory group is nested, and the option a mandatory group contributes is the one the catalogue names. What units receive today does not change beyond the members that were missing.
criteria: Issue criterion 1: adding `Zacharias the Everliving` to a fresh roster creates `Magic Level 4` (`799b-f6a5-b38c-b0c2`), held in group `Wizard Level` nested inside group `Magic`; `Zombie Dragon` and the six Bloodline powers on the same card still appear exactly once each.

Issue criterion 2: where a group names a `defaultSelectionEntryId` that matches one of its own options, that option is the one created; where the attribute is absent or points at nothing (as `Wizard Level`'s `42d9-cebe-18d5-cdbd` does), what is created is unchanged from today.
Issue criterion 7: the section tree, the section titles and the per-card row multiset are unchanged across the fixture catalogues' unit cards, except where a member that was missing is now created.
The price a card shows before a unit is recruited still matches what recruiting it actually costs.
The change is measured through the production recruitment path, not only through a test seam.

# Increment 1 — mandatory members are created at any group depth (defect A only)

## The defect, exactly

`populateChildren` (`src/roster/selectionFactory.js:69-83`) walks a resolved
definition's direct members and then `def.selectionEntryGroups` — one group
level. A group nested inside another group is never visited. On
`Zacharias the Everliving` (`1c05-5813-2f0c-f878`, Vampire Counts definitive)
the group `Magic` (`fe61-20a7-8126-d5b9`) carries no constraints at all, so its
child group `Wizard Level` (`af1f-355f-236b-a64f`, min 1 / max 1) is never
reached and its member `Magic Level 4` (`799b-f6a5-b38c-b0c2`, own min 1) is
never created. `Zombie Dragon` is created because its group `Mounts` sits at
depth 0.

Increment 1 fixes only this. Defect (B) — rendering an unmet obligation as
outstanding — belongs to a later increment; nothing in this increment touches
`src/components/`, `src/roster/selectionBehavior.js` or the CSS.

## What changes

### 1. `src/roster/selectionMembers.js` — one shared derivation of the walk

Add one exported function; this file already owns "which member a mandatory
group contributes" and is imported by both the factory and the cost estimate.

    /**
     * The mandatory children a resolved definition contributes when it is
     * recruited: direct members with a min of their own, plus the contribution
     * of every selection-entry group below it, at any depth.
     *
     * @param {object} def   the RESOLVED definition (or group) to walk.
     * @param {(defOrGroup: object) => number} minOf  the caller's reading of a
     *   min constraint (raw in the factory without a context, effective with
     *   one; always effective in the cost estimate). Returns 0 for no min.
     * @returns {Array<{ def: object, count: number }>} in creation order.
     */
    export function mandatoryChildrenOf(def, minOf)

Rules of the walk, in full:

- Direct members (`memberDefsOf(def)`, i.e. `selectionEntries` before
  `entryLinks`): every member whose `minOf` is > 0 contributes once, with its
  own min as the count. Unchanged from today.
- Groups: descend `selectionEntryGroups` recursively, **unconditionally** —
  descent is never gated on a group's own min, because `Magic` carries none and
  `Wizard Level` beneath it must still be reached.
- What a single group contributes is today's rule, applied at whatever depth
  the group sits:
  - `minOf(group) <= 0`, or `memberDefsOf(group)` empty → the group itself
    contributes nothing (its nested groups are still descended into);
  - else, if at least one direct member has `minOf > 0` → those members, each
    once with its own min ("itemised", `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §9.1);
  - else → `resolveGroupDefaultMember(group)` once, with the group's min as the
    count (§7.1: the named `defaultSelectionEntryId` if it matches one of the
    group's own members, otherwise the first member).
- A group contributes only its own direct members; a nested group's members are
  the nested group's business.
- Order: direct members first, then the groups in document order, each group's
  own contribution before the contributions of the groups nested inside it.
  Order carries no display meaning — a card's rows come from the report, not
  from roster order — but keeping it stable leaves every tree that gains
  nothing byte-identical to today's.

The walk is pure and does not resolve anything: it hands back catalogue
definitions and counts, and each caller does what it does with them.

### 2. `src/roster/selectionFactory.js`

`populateChildren` becomes one call:

    mandatoryChildrenOf(def, member => getMinConstraintValue(member, evaluationContext))
      .forEach(({ def: childDef, count }) => addMandatoryChild({ ..., childDef, count, ... }));

`populateMandatoryMembers` disappears into the shared walk;
`getMinConstraintValue` stays where it is and keeps its semantics (raw min
without an `evaluationContext`, modifier-adjusted with one), so the
effective-min behaviour of issue 02 is untouched. `addMandatoryChild` keeps
tolerating a `childDef` that does not resolve (`createSelectionFromDef` returns
null and the child is skipped) and keeps tolerating a null `childDef` from an
empty group. Update the German doc comment above `populateChildren` to say that
groups are walked at any depth and that a group's own min gates only what that
group contributes, never whether it is descended into — write the added
sentences in English, as the newer comments in this repo are.

### 3. `src/roster/rosterCounter.js` — the pre-recruit price moves with it

`getOptionDisplayCost` mirrors the factory's population rule by hand in its
steps 2, 3 and 4 (lines 114-139) and today stops at one group level, exactly as
the factory did. Replace those three blocks with the same walk:

    mandatoryChildrenOf(resolved, effectiveMin).forEach(({ def: child, count }) => {
      total += getOptionDisplayCost(system, child, costLimitType, ctx) * count;
    });

`effectiveMin` is the local helper already defined there (lines 107-112) and
keeps its own semantics, so nothing about modifier-adjusted minimums changes.
Two consequences, both intended:

- nested mandatory members are now priced, so the estimate keeps matching what
  recruiting actually costs (the contract `rosterCounter.mandatoryGroupDefault.test.js`
  already pins for the depth-0 case);
- an **itemised** group is now priced as the factory populates it (each member
  with its own min) instead of as `defaultMember × groupMin`. That divergence
  exists on the current tree and this change removes it. It is reachable in the
  fixtures: `0-1 Hill Goblins`' nested `Weapons` group would otherwise be priced
  with `Great Weapon` while the factory creates the free `Hand Weapon`.

### 4. `src/hooks/useRoster.js` — no change

Checked, against the codemap's note: `addUnit` already threads the
`evaluationContext` into the shared factory, and issue 0138's auto-add effect
(lines 209-231) works on force-level list rules through
`findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections`, never on a unit's children. A member
the factory now creates inside a unit cannot be added a second time there. The
production path needs nothing.

## Decisions, and what was rejected

- **A group's own min gates its members; nesting only gates reachability.**
  This is today's rule, applied at any depth, and it is the whole change.
  Rejected: populating every member with `min > 0` regardless of its group's min
  (a literal reading of §9.1). On Zacharias alone that would create the five
  `Equipment` members (`Handweapon`, `Circlet of Rathek`, `Book of Nagash`,
  `Scrolls of Semhtep`, `Staff of Kaphamon` — the `Equipment` group,
  `51b6-e84e-071d-54e2`, carries no constraints) and `Lore of Necromancy` (its
  group `Lores of Magic`, `3240-32da-ecd5-ee0f`, has a max but no min). Those
  are precisely the unmet obligations the issue counts among its 83 and that the
  later increment must render as outstanding; creating them here would empty out
  that increment and would go well past "what units receive today does not
  change beyond the members that were missing".
- **Descent is not gated on the group's min.** Rejected: descending only into
  groups that are themselves mandatory — `Magic` has no min, so `Wizard Level`
  would stay unreachable and criterion 1 would fail.
- **The walk is shared with the cost estimate rather than duplicated.**
  Rejected: recursing in the factory only. The two would then disagree on every
  newly reached nested group, which the increment's own criterion on the price
  forbids. (`selectionMembers.js` names ADR-0022 for this single-source rule;
  that ADR is marked *Superseded by ADR-0035*, so keep the principle as the code
  states it and do not cite 0022 as live.)
- **Group-typed links stay members.** An `entryLink type="selectionEntryGroup"`
  (e.g. Azhag's `Show Spells` links to `LittleWaaagh`/`Big Waaagh`) is kept in
  `entryLinks` by the parser and is treated as an ordinary member by
  `memberDefsOf` today. The walk descends `selectionEntryGroups` only, so that
  classification is untouched. No criterion needs it and no fixture has a
  mandatory nested group behind such a link; changing it would move rows, which
  criterion 7 forbids.

## What this actually creates, measured on the six fixture catalogues

A static scan of the raw XML of the six fixture catalogues (the three under
`src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and the three under
`src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`) for groups whose immediate parent is a group and
whose own min is > 0 — i.e. exactly the sites this change newly reaches — finds
four, and no more:

1. `Vampire Counts (6th definitive edition).cat` — `Wizard Level` (min 1) in
   `Magic`, on the unit `Zacharias the Everliving`: itemised, creates
   `Magic Level 4` × 1. Its `defaultSelectionEntryId="42d9-cebe-18d5-cdbd"`
   matches no member and is never consulted, because the itemised branch wins.
2. `Orcs and goblins (6th definitive edition).cat` — `Weapons` (min 1, max 2) in
   `Weapons and Armour`, on the unit `0-1 Hill Goblins` (`f23f-1816-93a7-3059`,
   `hidden="true"` but still a `type="unit"` entry of the catalogue and one of
   the 208 cards): itemised, creates `Hand Weapon` × 1 (`642a-7409-f1c0-4bd5`,
   the only member carrying a min).
3. `Vampire Counts (6th definitive edition).cat` — `Grimoire Necronium` (min 1)
   in `Magic Items`, on the **upgrade** entry `Melkhior the Ancient`: choose-one,
   creates its first member `1. Invocation of Nehek` × 1. Not a unit card;
   reached only when that entry is itself recruited as a sub-selection.
4. `Vampire Counts (6th definitive edition).cat` — `0. Signature spell` (min 1)
   in the shared group `Lore of High Magic`: choose-one, first member. Not
   under a unit entry.

So of the 208 unit cards, exactly two gain a member. Everything else in those
catalogues is untouched — which is what makes criterion 7 checkable at all. Two
things the scan also settles, both of which would otherwise look like the change
misfiring:

- `Level 2 Shaman` on `Azhag the Slaughterer` is **already** created today and
  stays that way: its group `Magic Level` hangs under the *entry*
  `The Crown of Sorcery`, not under another group, and the factory recurses
  through entries via `createSelectionFromDef`.
- `Zacharias`'s six Bloodline powers come from the depth-0 group
  `Bloodline (Necrarch)` (min 6, six members each min 1, itemised) and are
  untouched.

## Out of scope for this increment

The card's rendering of an unmet obligation, `selectionBehavior.js`, the three
render paths, `SelectionConfigurator.mandatoryInCappedGroup.test.jsx`'s five
`Lore of Necromancy` assertions, the CSS, i18n, the evaluator, and the version
bump in `package.json`. The issue file's own sections are the caller's to close.

## What this increment builds

One rule, written the same way on all three render paths of a unit card: **an obligation the roster already holds is taken and locked; an obligation it does not hold is an ordinary open offer.** Today the three paths derive "mandatory" from `effectiveMin === effectiveMax > 0` alone and render that as checked-and-disabled, whether or not the obligation is met.

### Measured state of the tree (throwaway sweep over the six fixture catalogues, 208 unit cards, on this branch, 2026-08-12)

Re-measured as the increment asks, because the issue's numbers predate both issue 0147 and inc-1:

- 3320 rendered option rows (the issue recorded 3329 before 0147 hid the `Lores of Magic` groups).
- **73 rows on 32 cards carry `isMandatoryUnmet: true`** (the issue recorded 83 on 36). All 73 have `effectiveMin === effectiveMax > 0`, `current: 0`, `anchorKind: mandatoryPhantom` and **`isBlocked: false`** — the report says every one of them is open.
  - 70 render as a **checkbox**, all `checked=true disabled=true` today: 63 inside a group, 7 standalone.
  - 3 render as a **quantity stepper** (min===max of 2, 3 and 5; quantity 0; `+` already enabled — the three rows the issue says can already be clicked): 2 standalone, 1 in a group.
  - **0 render as a radio.** The six unmet radios the issue counted were the `Lore of Necromancy` rows, which issue 0147 established are hidden and no longer render at all. The radio branch therefore has no case in the fixture data and must be pinned synthetically.
- **281 rows are mandatory and met**: 255 checkbox (`checked+disabled`), 7 radio (`checked+disabled`), 12 quantity steppers (quantity === min, `-` already disabled), 7 rows that render an *Add* button instead of a control (`isIndependentSubUnit`, e.g. sub-unit rows) — those have no taken/not-taken control at all.
- Only **2 sections across all 208 cards** carry `option-group-header--error`, both the `Herd` group of `Night Goblin Squig Herd` (definitive and legacy): group anchor `effectiveMin 10`, `current 3`, `isMandatoryUnmet: true`. Inside are two unchecked checkboxes and the stepper row `Night Goblin` at quantity 3 (its own slot: min 3, no max, met). **No checked checkbox or radio sits inside an error-styled section today.**
- Criterion 4's named rows all exist and are met after inc-1: `Zombie Dragon` and `Magic Level 4` on `Zacharias the Everliving` (both radios in a capped group), `Level 4 Shaman` on `Wurrzag Ud Ura Zahubu`, `Grom's Chariot` and `The Axe of Grom: Elf-Biter` on the card named **`Grom the Paunch of Misty Mountain`**, `Level 2 Shaman` on `Azhag the Slaughterer` (all radios), `Hand Weapon` on `0-1 Hill Goblins` (group checkbox), and `Bulak's Bloody Armour` on `Morglum Necksnapper`, whose row is labelled **`Bulak's Bloody Armour (Magic Armour)`** — a radio in `Magic Items (Max: 1)` whose slot is `isBlocked: true`, so its lock must come from the met obligation, not from availability.

### The design

`isMandatoryUnmet` is the discriminator, per the issue's own decision (`current` and `anchorKind` are not). It enters the two classifiers, which keep owning the constraint decision (ADR 0029: the components decide nothing about constraints themselves).

**1. `src/roster/selectionBehavior.js`** — both classifiers take the slot's `isMandatoryUnmet` and return one new flag next to the existing ones:

```js
export function classifyGroupItem({
  minLimit, maxLimit, hasMaxConstraint, isCollective,
  isRepeatableByGroupModifier, groupSingleChoice, isMandatoryUnmet = false
}) {
  const isMandatory = minLimit > 0 && minLimit === maxLimit;
  const isMandatoryMet = isMandatory && !isMandatoryUnmet;
  ...
  return { isMandatory, isMandatoryMet, isRadio, hasQuantitySignal, isExplicitlyMulti, isBinary };
}

export function classifyStandaloneOption({ minLimit, maxLimit, isMandatoryUnmet = false }) {
  const isMandatory = minLimit > 0 && minLimit === maxLimit;
  return { isMandatory, isMandatoryMet: isMandatory && !isMandatoryUnmet, isBinary: maxLimit === 1 };
}
```

`isMandatory` keeps its meaning (a catalogue reading: min===max>0) and stays in the return so the classifiers stay honest about the two different facts; only `isMandatoryMet` drives display. The parameter defaults to `false` on purpose: a caller with a hand-built capability that lacks the field keeps today's behaviour rather than silently unlocking a row. The JSDoc `@param`/`@returns` blocks must be extended in the same edit — `npm run typecheck` checks these blocks (`checkJs`), and every call site destructures the new key.

**2. The three render paths** (`OptionGroup.jsx` checkbox branch, `OptionGroup.jsx` radio branch, `SelectionConfigurator.jsx` standalone row). Each computes the same three expressions from its slot, and nothing else about "mandatory" appears in the JSX:

```js
const isMandatoryUnmet = capability.isMandatoryUnmet === true;   // straight from the report
// … pass isMandatoryUnmet into the classifier, take isMandatoryMet out of it
const isUnavailable = count === 0 && isSelectDisabled;           // unchanged
const isClickable   = !isMandatoryMet && !isUnavailable;         // was !isMandatory && …
// One rule on all three paths: what the effective minimum demands cannot be given
// back, and an obligation the roster already holds is exactly that case.
const canRemove     = count > minLimit && !isMandatoryMet;
```

and the controls read:

- binary control (group checkbox, group radio, standalone checkbox): `checked={count > 0 || isMandatoryMet}`, `disabled={count > 0 ? !canRemove : isSelectDisabled}`.
- the write handlers: an increase happens when `!isSelectDisabled` (the radio branch still calls `decreaseSelectedSiblings()` first); a decrease happens only when `canRemove`.
- quantity stepper `-` button: `disabled={!canRemove}` on **both** paths. On the standalone path this is the same predicate as today's `count <= minLimit` plus the met lock (no change for any measured row). On the group path it replaces `count === 0`, which never honoured a minimum at all.
- quantity stepper `+` button: unchanged on both paths (`isSelectDisabled` in the group, `isSelectDisabled || count >= maxLimit` standalone).
- the *Add* button of an independent sub-unit row: unchanged; it has no taken state to get wrong.

Why this is equivalent for every row that is not an obligation: with `minLimit === 0`, `canRemove` reduces to `count > 0`, so `disabled` reduces to today's `count === 0 && isSelectDisabled` and the stepper's `-` to today's `count === 0`.

What it changes, exhaustively over the fixture population:
- the 70 unmet checkbox rows render **unchecked and enabled**, and a click on the control or on the row writes `increaseCount(<carrier selection id>, <option>)`;
- the 3 unmet stepper rows keep their working `+` and gain a clickable row (`isClickable` no longer false);
- the 281 met rows are untouched: `isMandatoryMet` is true for them, so `checked` and `disabled` stay exactly as they are — including where the UI count and the report disagree, because `checked` keeps the `|| isMandatoryMet` term;
- exactly one further row changes across all 208 cards: `Night Goblin` on `Night Goblin Squig Herd` (group stepper, min 3, quantity 3) can no longer be decremented below its own minimum of 3. That is the standalone path's existing rule, now spelled the same way in the group, and it is what criterion 5 asks for.

**3. Comments that assert the old behaviour must be rewritten in the same edit**, or the file will contradict itself: `OptionGroup.jsx` header lines 26-28 ("eine offene Pflicht … rendert als angehakter, gesperrter Schalter"), the radio's inline justification at lines 297-301 (written for issue 0143, criterion 6), and the classifier docblocks in `selectionBehavior.js`. Cite `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §9.1 for the reading: BattleScribe creates what meets a minimum and then stops enforcing it, so an unmet minimum after creation is an open obligation, not a settled one.

**4. `src/styles/09-editor-options.css`** — delete the dead rule `.sub-selection-taken-hint` (lines 66-69); it has no user anywhere in the repository and its name claims exactly the state this issue removes. No new row vocabulary is added: the open obligation is already reported by the group header (`option-group-header--error`), the sidebar badge and the validation panel, and the issue records that no new vocabulary is needed.

### Options weighed and rejected

- **Make `isMandatory` itself mean "met"** (one-line change, every call site untouched). Rejected: the word would then mean two things across the codebase, and the classifier's own unit tests would keep passing while asserting something else.
- **Give the unmet row a visual marking of its own** (a red row, a hint chip, a new i18n string). Rejected: no criterion asks for it, the issue records that the app's existing vocabulary suffices, and the codemap puts `src/i18n/locales/*.json` out of scope.
- **Lock the group stepper's `-` only for a met mandatory (`!isMandatoryMet || count === 0`) instead of at the minimum.** Rejected: it would leave the group and standalone paths disagreeing for the min>0/max unbounded shape, which is precisely the disagreement criterion 5 names. The cost is one row in the whole fixture corpus.
- **Also clamp the group stepper's `+` with `count >= maxLimit`, as the standalone one does.** Rejected: `isBlocked` is the report's answer to "may this be raised" (ADR 0035), the clamp is redundant belt-and-braces, and adding it would change rows that have nothing to do with an obligation.
- **Measure criteria 3 and 6 inside the existing 0143 sweep file.** Rejected: that file is issue 0143's record and the increment requires it to stay green; this issue's measurements get their own sweep file with the same harness.

The tracker file `docs/issues/0145-.../issue.md` and the `package.json` version bump belong to the coordinator, not to the implementer. The project's screenshot rule for a UI-visible change is likewise the coordinator's step, and no command in the check list produces one.
